title: Target market
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:32Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The closest bank point, Identifying target markets, covers the choice between mass, segment and niche targeting, but the new point also asks for market size and trends in customer behaviour, which none of the bank cards teach, so it is a related but broader idea.

draft.title: Target market
card: A target market is the group of customers a business aims its products at. A business cannot suit everyone, so it chooses who it will serve.
the number of potential customers, or the total sales, in the group. It shows whether the group is big enough to earn a profit.
smaller groups inside a market, split by traits such as age, income, gender or location. A business picks the segment that suits its product.
changes in what customers do or want over time, such as buying more online. A business watches trends to see if its target market is growing or shrinking.
draft.remember: A target market is the group a business chooses, described by its size, its segments and its trends.

a.q: Priya opens a gym in Ballarat for people aged 60 and over. What does choosing this age group show?
opts: She has picked a market segment
She has measured the market size
She has found a customer trend
She has set a business objective
a.why: Age is a trait used to split a market into segments, and she has chosen one segment to serve. Market size would be the number of people in that group, which she has not stated.
a.clue: Age is one way to split a market into smaller groups.

b.q: A Geelong bakery finds that more people each year are buying gluten-free bread. Which description fits this finding?
opts: A trend in what customers want
b.why: The finding shows a change in customer behaviour over time, which is a trend. It is not market size, because it does not count the total number of customers or total sales. It is not a location segment, because no place is used to split the market.
b.clue: Look for the word that shows change over time.

a.best: She has picked a market segment

b.best: A trend in what customers want

check.summary: No problems found. The card, the remember line and both questions are accurate, match the study design and fit Year 11, and the explanations agree with the card.
